title: Perf-canary gates + alert thresholds for hardware tuning profile rollouts
creator: Talia Benson
description:
Goal
Add/adjust perf-canary gates and production alert thresholds specifically for enabling hardware tuning profiles (H100/L40S, B200 experimental) so we can:
- Catch regressions in p95/p99 latency, streaming stability, and error rates during staged rollouts
- Reduce false positives/noise versus current generic perf-canary thresholds
- Make it easy for oncall/SRE to attribute regressions to “profile enabled” vs unrelated runtime changes

Context
The profile pack is changing scheduler presets + kernel autoselect heuristics + KV cache budgeting. This has historically shifted the latency/throughput frontier (especially tail latency under mixed seq-len + streaming). We need SKU-aware bounds and explicit rollback criteria that match the intended “safe-by-default” envelope.

Scope
In scope
- Update perf-canary to segment results by:
  - GPU SKU (H100, L40S, B200)
  - profile selection status (enabled/disabled) and selected profile ID/version
  - workload class from the workload matrix runner (seq len bucket, concurrency, streaming/non-streaming)
- Add gating rules for PR builds and post-deploy canaries:
  - latency deltas (p50/p95/p99) relative to baseline
  - throughput deltas (tokens/sec) relative to baseline
  - error rate deltas (5xx, timeouts, OOM, “dropped stream”)
  - stability signals (retry rate, request cancellation rate, tail amplification during load)
- Create/adjust alert thresholds in production dashboards for rollout monitoring:
  - “profile-enabled pool vs control pool” comparisons
  - rollback triggers with clear oncall playbook

Out of scope
- New benchmark workloads (tracked in ENG-4827)
- Changes to runtime behavior itself (covered by ENG-4824/4825/4826 and related PRs)

Acceptance criteria
1) Perf-canary gating (pre-merge)
- For H100 and L40S canary runners:
  - p95 end-to-end latency regression must be <= +3% for the balanced profile on the standard workload matrix (streaming + non-streaming)
  - p99 regression must be <= +5% (tail regressions are the priority signal)
  - throughput (tokens/sec) must not regress more than -2% on decode-heavy workloads; prefill-heavy can trade off up to -5% if p95 improves (documented exception)
  - OOM rate must remain 0 on in-matrix tests (hard fail)
  - streaming “dropped stream” / stream reset rate must be within +0.05% absolute
- Gates must be SKU-aware (L40S has a different envelope due to memory constraints and guardrails; see ENG-4825)
- Gates must be less noisy than current defaults; target <5% false-positive gate failures week-over-week (measured via canary job history)

2) Post-deploy canary gating (staged rollout)
- When enabling a profile per pool/region, alerts + dashboards must show:
  - selected profile, override source, profile version (to disambiguate drift)
  - pool-level p95/p99, error rates, and retry rates against a control pool
- Rollback criteria must be explicit, automated where possible:
  - Roll back profile enablement if p95 increases >8% sustained for 15 minutes OR p99 increases >12% sustained for 15 minutes, with no corresponding throughput gain >5%
  - Immediate rollback if OOMs >0.2% of requests or timeouts >0.5% (15-min window)
  - Immediate rollback if streaming dropped stream rate >0.2% absolute increase

3) SRE sign-off
- SRE (Neha Kapoor org) to confirm:
  - thresholds are actionable
  - alert routing is correct (eng-oncall + eng-sre)
  - runbook links are present in alerts

Implementation plan
- Perf-canary
  - Extend perf-canary job to ingest the profile-selection metrics exposed by runtime (PR: sources/github/redwood/pr-22027-expose-profile-selection-metrics-and-debug-endpoint.json)
  - Update gates and baselines to be per-SKU + per-workload-class (consume runner artifact from benchmark-lab PR: sources/github/benchmark-lab/pr-1842-workload-matrix-runner-for-hardware-profiles.json)
  - Add "profile-enabled" vs "profile-disabled" comparisons for the same build to reduce variance

- Observability + Alerts
  - Add dashboard panels:
    - latency/throughput segmented by selected profile
    - tail-latency “fanout” view during rollout windows
    (PR: sources/github/observability-pack/pr-488-add-dashboard-panels-for-profile-selection-and-tail-latency.json)
  - Add alert rules:
    - Profile rollout regression: p95/p99 + error spikes in profile-enabled pool vs control pool
    - Streaming stability regression
    - OOM anomaly for L40S pools
  - Ensure alerts include:
    - pool/region, GPU SKU
    - current profile ID/version and override source
    - quick links: perf-canary run, dashboard, rollout runbook

Open questions / decisions
- Baseline definition: use last 7 days median of canary runs per SKU as baseline, but pin to specific runtime release branch for comparisons to avoid drift.
- Streaming gate: use dropped stream rate + client cancellation rate (cancellation can spike due to client timeouts; need to interpret alongside server p99).
- B200 gating: keep behind experimental flag; use looser initial thresholds (+8% p95, +15% p99) until we have stable fleet + runner variance characterized.

Links
- Perf-canary gates PR: sources/github/perf-canary/pr-731-add-gates-for-profile-rollout-latency-and-throughput.json
- Runtime metrics for profile selection: sources/github/redwood/pr-22027-expose-profile-selection-metrics-and-debug-endpoint.json
- Rollout runbook (WIP): sources/confluence/eng-serving-runtime/runbooks/rollout-runbook-hardware-tuning-profiles.json
- Known noise discussion (Slack): sources/slack/eng-runtime/1764307714-perf-canary-thresholds-too-noisy.json
- SRE rollback guardrails thread: sources/slack/eng-sre/1763810094-rollout-guardrails-and-rollback-criteria.json

Notes
- These gates should be calibrated to catch the specific failure modes we’ve already seen in early validation:
  - tail latency regressions from prefill/decode fairness tuning
  - L40S OOMs under long-context workloads
  - streaming instability under high concurrency

Deliverables
- Updated perf-canary thresholds (pre-merge + post-deploy)
- Updated dashboards + alert rules with profile-aware context
- SRE sign-off recorded in ticket
comments: 2025-11-19 (Kira Volkov): Drafted initial gate thresholds for H100/L40S based on last 2 weeks of canary variance. Key change: moving from single global p95 bound to per-SKU/per-workload bounds. Posted for review in #eng-sre and #eng-runtime.

2025-11-20 (Aisha Bello - SRE): +1 on SKU-aware bounds. Request: alerts must include a direct link to the "effective runtime config" dump and selected profile metrics; otherwise oncall can’t tell if this is a profile issue or unrelated load. Also, please add a hard-fail gate for any OOM in the perf suite runs (even if latency looks fine).

2025-11-22 (Kira Volkov): Updated plan: hard-fail on OOM; added streaming dropped-stream metric gate. Coordinating with Runtime to ensure metric names are stable and exported in canary builds (see PR-22027).

2025-11-25 (Sean Gallagher - SRE): For rollback criteria, we need a sustained-window trigger to avoid flapping. Proposed: 15 min sustained regression + minimum request volume threshold. Also: route alerts to eng-oncall with eng-sre as secondary; include runbook section anchors in alert annotations.

2025-11-27 (Kira Volkov): Implemented sustained-window + min volume checks in alert rules. Added annotations: profile_id, profile_version, override_source, pool, region, sku. Linked rollout runbook. Preparing perf-canary PR.

2025-12-02 (Allison Grant): Dashboard panels look good. Please ensure the alert names and labels match observability standards (service=runtime, component=profile-pack, severity=page vs ticket). Also, separate L40S OOM alert from generic OOM since we expect different memory behavior under guardrails.
2025-12-04 (Kira Volkov): Split L40S OOM alert, added standard labels, and updated gating docs in perf-canary repo. PR up: perf-canary/pr-731. Requesting SRE sign-off.

2025-12-06 (Neha Kapoor - SRE sponsor): Sign-off granted with condition: B200 remains experimental with looser gates until runner variance is characterized; any B200 enablement requires control pool comparison and explicit rollback owner. Marking approved for H100/L40S rollout.

2025-12-10 (Kira Volkov): Merged perf-canary changes and alert updates. Recorded final thresholds and rollback criteria in the rollout runbook. Closing ticket; follow-up to tighten B200 bounds once we have ≥2 weeks stable canary history.
